usage: This is the standard greeting used from late afternoon until late at night in formal and broadcast contexts. It is universally understood across the Arab world and remains unchanged regardless of the gender or number of people being addressed. It is frequently used to open news broadcasts, formal speeches, and evening meetings.

variants.label: standard
variants.note: The default phrase used for anyone, regardless of gender or number.

variants.label: highly formal to a group
variants.note: Used by news anchors, hosts, or public speakers addressing an audience.

variants.label: highly formal to a man
variants.note: A formal wish directed at a single male.

variants.label: highly formal to a woman
variants.note: A formal wish directed at a single female.

examples.transliteration: masaa' al-khayr ayyuhaa as-sayyidaat wa as-saadah.

examples.arabic: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ، هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي التَّحَدُّثُ مَعَ الْمُدِيرِ؟
examples.transliteration: masaa' al-khayr, hal yumkinunii at-ta7adduth ma3a al-mudiir?
examples.english: Good evening, may I speak with the manager?

examples.arabic: قَالَ الْمُذِيعُ: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ وَأَهْلاً بِكُمْ فِي نَشْرَةِ الْأَخْبَارِ.
examples.transliteration: qaala al-mudhii3: masaa' al-khayr wa ahlan bikum fii nashrat al-akhbaar.
examples.english: The announcer said: Good evening and welcome to the news broadcast.
